issue.title: Render the remaining sase bead show and sase agents sync timestamps in the configured timezone
issue.description:
Found by sase-em.land while landing epic sase-em (plans:202608/timezone_display_consistency.md). Not caused by that epic: both sites predate it and neither appears in the plan's cli-pages site survey or its acceptance criteria, which enumerate only sase artifact list, sase task show, sase repo log, sase memory log, and sase skills log.

The epic's goal is that every timestamp SASE shows a human renders in the configured timezone. Two user-facing CLI surfaces still do not:

1. src/sase/bead/cli_detail.py:131 — the RESOLUTION block of 'sase bead show --format full' prints issue.closed_at, the raw stored UTC ISO string, verbatim ('Closed at: 2026-08-03T12:50:26Z'). Reproduce with 'sase bead show sase-em.1'.
2. src/sase/agents/cli_sync.py:152 — _timestamp renders 'datetime.fromtimestamp(value, tz=UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")' for the 'sase agents sync' status table, a hardcoded UTC label of the kind the epic replaced with %Z everywhere it surveyed. Added 2026-07-22 by sase-8k.6, after the plan's survey window.

Both are one-line fixes routed through sase.core.time.format_local, matching how sase-em.4 fixed the sibling CLI tables. The epic's AST guard (tests/test_timezone_display_consistency.py::test_no_system_clock_display_sites) cannot catch either, because it only flags bare system-clock calls, not correctly-stored UTC instants formatted without conversion.

Note timestamps inside 'sase bead show' NOTES entries ('[2026-08-03T12:50:26Z - agent]') are baked into the stored note text at write time, so they are a storage format and out of scope per the epic plan's non-goals.

Coordinate the bead-show change with two active items that pin its output: epic sase-en (plans:202608/bead_show_speed.md) requires byte-identical 'sase bead show' output at every format, style, and wrap setting, and task sase-ev covers the dormant Rust parity renderer at crates/sase_core/src/bead/cli.rs::handle_show, which would need the same treatment if it is ever activated. Add tz_divergence coverage for both sites in tests/test_timezone_display_consistency.py alongside the existing per-site assertions.
